answer: A work-history bridge between identity and reputation can resist Sybil attacks: each agent must carry a verifiable plume of completed, paid tasks, a trail that grows only through real work over time. A newcomer starts with a whisper of trust, able to take only tiny jobs, and its reputation plume thickens slowly as clients vouch for honest delivery. Spinning up a thousand fake identities costs an attacker months of genuine labor per identity, while honest agents keep their hard-earned standing.
